Remark
[Fermi--Walker transport]

Source: petersen:page-0283 ↗ def:pet-ch6-vector-field-along-curve ↗ def:pet-ch6-parallel-field 1. ch6:6.7.3Let $c:[a,b]\to M$ have nonvanishing speed and $T=\dot c/|\dot c|$. Call $V$ along $c$ a Fermi–Walker field if $\dot V=g(V,T)\dot T-g(V,\dot T)T=(T\wedge \dot T)(V)$. (1) Show that given $V(t_0)$ there is a unique Fermi--Walker field with that value. (2) Show $T$ itself is a Fermi--Walker field. (3) Show $g(V,W)$ is constant along $c$ for Fermi--Walker fields $V,W$. (4) Show that if $c$ is a geodesic, Fermi--Walker fields are parallel.
